title: Molossians
capsule: The Molossians were a Greek-speaking tribal people of Epirus whose ruling Aeacid dynasty — claiming descent from Achilles through Neoptolemus — unified Epirus around 370 BC and forged a dynastic alliance with Macedon when Olympias, a Molossian princess, married Philip II in 357 BC. King Pyrrhus (r. 306–272 BC), regarded as one of the greatest generals of antiquity, defeated Rome at Heraclea (280 BC) and Asculum (279 BC) at prohibitive cost, giving the language the phrase 'Pyrrhic victory.' After the Aeacid line ended with the murder of Deidamia II in 233 BC, the Molossians joined the Epirote League; siding with Macedonia against Rome in the Third Macedonian War, they suffered the enslavement of approximately 150,000 Epirotes by Roman forces in 167 BC, effectively annihilating their community as a political entity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Molossian heartland in northwestern Epirus is documented through ancient geographers and inscriptions; tribal sub-boundaries and the precise extent of Pyrrhus's Epirote kingdom remain debated.
